subject: Checking model assumptions post model fit

messages.author: 00d33217ce2031fe
messages.subject: Checking model assumptions post model fit
parts:
Greetings all,

Is there a simple way to check that a fitted model meets the assumptions of linearity?  Namely I wish to ensure that my data and the path model used to fit the data meet the assumptions of linearity, normally distributed errors, and homogeneity of variance.  I'd like to do this post model-fit. 

Any information on how to go about this would be of tremendous help!

Thanks!

-Tim

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Checking model assumptions post model fit
parts: I wish to ensure that my data and the path model used to fit the data meet the assumptions of linearity, normally distributed errors, and homogeneity of variance.

In covariance structure analysis, "residuals" are differences between observed and expected (model-implied, predicted) elements of the covariance matrix, not differences between observed and expected values of the outcome(s) for each row of data.  If you want to do that kind of residual analysis (assuming you only have observed variables in your path analysis), you can either use the estimates to calculate predicted values and then residuals, or you can just fit a regression model to each outcome and extract the residuals like you would after running regressions using lm().
